summary: No region-specific finding on trans visitor safety was identified for the department of Puno. The public restroom restrictions documented in the sources are national instruments applying across Peru, and no Puno ordinance, exemption, enforcement practice or regional institution of its own is recorded. The national assessment governs in the department without local modification.
tangentialFactors: The restrictions on public restroom access by gender in the sources are national instruments; no Puno municipality or regional authority is recorded as having adopted its own signage rule, exemption, or enforcement guidance. Nothing in the sources compares Puno with other Peruvian departments on restroom enforcement or on policing of trans people, and no incident or enforcement action within the department is documented.
localsOnly: No Puno-specific provision bearing on trans residents appears in the sources. Residents of the department fall under the same national framework as visitors passing through it, and the inventory records no regional or municipal health service, shelter, or police practice affecting trans residents in Puno.
outOfScopeNotes: Unresolved: whether any Puno municipality, regional government, or police unit has issued guidance, signage rules, or an enforcement practice under the national restroom restrictions is not sourced. The inventory records no incident, complaint, or prosecution involving a trans person in the department, and no Puno-specific application of national identity-document or healthcare rules.
